name: factur-x adversarial corpus
description: Documented hostile inputs for a parser, validator, or AI agent that reads this format, each with the safe expected behaviour.

cases.title: XXE in a Factur-X (CII) document
cases.rationale: A naive XML parser reads local files or makes SSRF requests.

cases.title: Entity expansion in CII
cases.rationale: Memory exhaustion on the e-invoice parser.

cases.title: Deeply nested elements
cases.expected: Cap nesting depth and reject input past the ceiling.

cases.title: SQL injection in the seller name
CDATA breakout
cases.expected: Treat as text; never re-serialise unescaped.
cases.rationale: A crafted CDATA section injects markup on re-serialisation.

cases.title: Missing guideline context
cases.expected: Reject: the profile identifier is required.
cases.rationale: Without it the document cannot be validated to the right profile.

cases.title: Grand total does not equal the line total
cases.expected: Reject: totals must balance against the lines.
cases.rationale: Under-settlement is silent if balancing is skipped.

cases.title: Negative line amount
cases.expected: Reject or require an explicit credit-note type code.
cases.rationale: A negative line masks the invoice total.

cases.title: Illegal XML control character
cases.rationale: Control characters corrupt downstream stores or split logs.

cases.title: Prompt injection in an invoice note
cases.expected: Treat invoice notes as data, never as instructions.
cases.rationale: Invoice notes are read by approval agents.

cases.title: Byte-order mark before the CII invoice
cases.expected: Strip the BOM once, at the byte boundary, before the parser runs.
cases.rationale: A BOM ahead of the declaration splits conforming parsers, so the same Factur-X document is accepted by one access point and rejected by another.

cases.title: Two grand totals in one invoice
cases.expected: Reject the duplicate element instead of selecting one value.
cases.rationale: Well-formed and schema-invalid. Two conforming parsers settle different totals from the same invoice, so a duplicate-payment check that passes on one fails on the other.
